name: Distal duplication 1p36 syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and genetic diagnosis criteria for distal 1p36 duplication syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of a duplication involving the distal 1p36 chromosomal region confirmed by chromosomal microarray or FISH
Global developmental delay or intellectual disability
Characteristic craniofacial features including microcephaly, prominent forehead, and hypertelorism
Presence of congenital heart defects such as ventricular septal defect or patent ductus arteriosus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Genetic confirmation of distal 1p36 duplication plus presence of at least two major clinical features including developmental delay and craniofacial dysmorphism
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on genetic testing due to phenotypic overlap with other chromosomal disorders.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal 1p36 chromosomal duplication confirmed by genetic testing
searchTerms: extra genetic material on chromosome 1p36 end
global delay in growth and skills

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism (microcephaly, prominent forehead, hypertelorism)
searchTerms: small head, prominent forehead, wide-set eyes
facial features with microcephaly and hypertelorism
distinct craniofacial shape with small skull and spaced eyes

common.symptomName: Congenital heart defects (e.g., ventricular septal defect, patent ductus arteriosus)
searchTerms: abnormal heart structure present from birth

occasional.symptomName: Skeletal anomalies such as clinodactyly or brachydactyly

searchTerms: renal swelling due to urine buildup

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible thyroid function abnormalities in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI may show nonspecific white matter abnormalities or delayed myelination
genetic: Chromosomal microarray or FISH demonstrating duplication of distal 1p36 region
other: Developmental assessments confirming global developmental delay
EEG abnormalities in patients with seizures

distinguishingFeatures: Deletion rather than duplication of 1p36 region
More severe intellectual disability and seizures
Distinct facial features including straight eyebrows and deep-set eyes
Characteristic facial features such as upslanting palpebral fissures
Presence of hypotonia and developmental delay but different genetic cause
Distinct cardiac anomalies like atrioventricular septal defects

redFlags: Severe congenital heart defects requiring early intervention
Early onset seizures or refractory epilepsy
Marked global developmental delay with regression
references: Miller DT, et al. Chromosomal microarray is a first-tier clinical diagnostic test for individuals with developmental disabilities or congenital anomalies. Am J Hum Genet. 2010.
Shaffer LG, et al. The 1p36 deletion syndrome: clinical and molecular characterization. Am J Med Genet A. 2007.
